replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That's a really interesting firsthand observation. Bazaruto Archipelago National Park was first established in 1971, and the protected area was expanded to cover the entire archipelago in 2001. Of course, being officially protected doesn't always mean illegal or unsustainable practices disappear overnight. What you saw is an important reminder of the gap that can exist between protection on paper and what happens on the ground. Thanks for sharing your experience.

comments.author: @BeyondTheMapTV1
comments.text: What makes Bazaruto especially interesting is that conservation here cannot simply mean removing people from nature. 🌊🇲🇿 Local families have depended on fishing, tides and marine resources for generations, while the same reefs and seagrass now need protection from overuse. The real challenge is finding a balance where wildlife survives without making traditional island life economically impossible.
